record.title: Rishtan–Kaytpas inherited closure partially lifted in September 2017
record.scope: Rishtan–Kaytpas checkpoint; partial restoration for Kyrgyz and Uzbek citizens
record.direction: Citizen crossing between Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan in both directions.
record.movement: People, vehicles and goods in the 2013 closure statement; 2017 restoration explicitly concerns Kyrgyz and Uzbek citizens.
record.exceptions: 2017 citizen passage limited to 07:00–19:00; freight and third-country eligibility not established.
record.enforcement: Contemporary official closure statement and later reporter/interview evidence of partial restoration.
record.consequences: Shorter route remained unavailable to Sokh through-travellers because Apkan was still closed.
record.relationship: Separate checkpoint phase preceding CC026 (post-August-2019 Sokh route restriction); not a duplicate of Dostuk, Baymak or Madaniyat. Apkan continued closure remains follow-up lead.
record.official_rationale: Kyrgyz Border Service cited stabilization after the January 2013 Charbak incident.
record.context: Local border conflict and subsequent negotiations. Reopening Kaytpas did not restore the full route to Sokh because Apkan remained closed. A September19 report attributes a brief earlier Kaytpas opening and reclosure to a Batken official; September25 is therefore a documented later partial restoration, not established first admission since2013.
record.uncertainty: January 2013 onset is month precision. No proof of uninterrupted identical closure from 2013 to 2017. Reopening applies only to specified citizen movement at Kaytpas, not all goods or the full Sokh route. September19 source reports an intermediate opening/reclosure, without exact dates or matched traffic categories. Do not treat September25 as the first lifting of the inherited closure or calculate a 2013–2017 continuous spell.

historical.duration_note: No exact start or continuous movement-matched interval.
